page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 64 GB of memory configured at 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-thread performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2908.08 placing in the top 25% tier. PassMark memory testing also ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2894.0, supported by uncached large-block read bandwidth of 78.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 48.32 GB/sec. Broader multicore compute metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 10599.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23917.02, demonstrate stable mid-range throughput across compilation, image manipulation, and general multi-threaded execution.

Without integrated local NVMe storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, the instance trades standalone persistence and external networking conveniences for dedicated compute and memory density. This design yields balanced resource efficiency for processing-centric services, avoiding overhead associated with unneeded hardware accelerators.

The c2d-standard-16 is well-suited for compute-bound and memory-balanced enterprise tasks, such as continuous integration builds, static web serving fleets, middle-tier application microservices, and small-scale language model inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-16 is a compute-optimized instance delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features 64 GB of RAM, a 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX, AES, and SHA. It incorporates no GPUs and provides no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark results show strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests and competitive memory handling in PassMark assessments, alongside steady mid-tier multicore processing results across Geekbench suites. Lacking local storage arrays and specialized accelerators, it offers an efficient compute-to-memory configuration focused on pure CPU tasks. The instance aligns well with continuous integration compilation, medium-scale web application serving, batch data processing, and lightweight inference workloads.
